$comment: Reviewable source of truth for the live GitHub merge-boundary rules (#162).
M0 uses repository Rulesets, not classic branch protection. The fields under
`branches` retain the classic request vocabulary where it maps cleanly so the
existing offline workflow/check audit remains useful; `ruleset` records the
Ruleset-only semantics needed to reconstruct the live settings.
The live topology is topic branches -> develop -> main. `integration` is retired.
Accepted topic-branch prefixes (#381). This is the one source: README,
CONTRIBUTING, docs/WAYS-OF-WORKING.md and the workflows' push filters
are validated against it by tests/test_branch_policy.py. Push-triggered
gates must cover every prefix documented here, and PR gates run
regardless of source prefix (pull_request triggers are unfiltered).
Checks that report only on main-based PRs.
Canonical development branch. PR-gated, zero approvals, linear history.

contexts: JS supply chain (npm audit + GuardDog + policy gate)

$comment: Release/promotion branch. Ordinary changes reach main through develop -> main PRs.
One approval is required. Merge commits are intentionally allowed as release markers;
linear history is therefore not required on main. Creation is restricted.

contexts: JS supply chain (npm audit + GuardDog + policy gate)

develop: bypass actors are ['Organizatio.reason: The live develop ruleset grants five GitHub App integrations an always-bypass and a maintain-role actor (RepositoryRole 4) that the declared policy does not name. Recorded rather than reconciled: an integration that still publishes required statuses cannot simply be dropped from the ruleset without risking the queue, and adding it to the policy would bless an actor nobody reviewed here. Confirm which apps still need bypass and either name them in the policy or remove them from the ruleset (#564).

develop: classic branch protection is ac.reason: GitHub applies classic protection on develop alongside the ruleset, and the classic surface does not block branch/tag creation while the ruleset's `creation` rule does. The effective boundary is the intersection, so the stricter ruleset rule holds today - but a second surface with different flags is exactly where a later change quietly stops meaning what the policy says. Aligning or retiring the classic surface is a live-settings change owned by #564.

develop: dismiss_stale_reviews is True i.reason: The policy and the classic develop protection both dismiss stale reviews; the live ruleset does not, so a reader of the ruleset alone concludes approvals survive a push that replaces the diff. Classic protection still enforces dismissal on develop today, which is why this is recorded and not an outage - but the declared mechanism (ADR-095 rulesets) does not do what the policy declares. Aligning the ruleset is a live-settings change owned by #564.

develop: merge queue differs: check_resp.reason: .github/merge-queue.json records the reviewed batching posture (ALLGREEN, max_entries_to_build 3, max_entries_to_merge 3, 2-minute group wait, 60-minute timeout; #1438/#1477) and scripts/check-required-checks.py fails closed on anything wider. The live queue is wider on all five of those parameters (HEADGREEN, 10, 15, 5 minutes, 90 minutes). Recorded so the reviewed posture and the enforced one cannot be mistaken for each other: widening the live queue past the reviewed cap without editing the gate is the exact failure #1438 closed, and reconciling the two is the merge-policy program's (#160/#162) decision, not this file's.

develop: required checks the live rulese.reason: The live develop ruleset requires nine checks the policy lists as advisory, so they gate merges although the merge contract does not declare them. Stricter than declared is still drift: a check required by accident can be removed by accident, and the advisory reasons in this file then describe a contract GitHub is not enforcing. #564 owns reconciling the declared set with the live set; do not edit either side just to make this line vanish.

main: required checks the live ruleset r.reason: The live main ruleset requires the autonomous-merge admissibility check while the declared policy does not list it among main's required contexts: its producer is a pull_request_target workflow, outside the pull_request job graph this gate walks, so declaring it as an ordinary context would fail the offline audit that every required context has a job. It is recorded instead, together with the fact below that no producer currently exists.

main: the live ruleset requires 'autonom.reason: PERMANENT-EXPECTED RISK: the producer .github/workflows/autonomous-merge.yml was deleted in 14a67ddf5a ('ci: disable autonomous merge safety gate for now', 2026-08-28) and has not been restored, while the live main ruleset still requires its check name. Until a producer exists, a PR targeting main waits on a check that never reports - the failure this gate exists to prevent. Re-enabling the trusted gate or removing the requirement are both trusted-surface decisions (AUTONOMOUS-MERGES.md: the introducing PR requires a human merge), so it is recorded with an owner rather than resolved by a gate.

develop: required checks the policy decl.reason: The live develop ruleset does not yet require these policy-declared checks. The four coverage producer jobs joined the develop merge contract on 2026-11-28 (parallel coverage producers, homie1/ci-speed-20261128) alongside six checks already drifting the same way. Recorded rather than reconciled: updating the live ruleset needs the ops/protection-sync flow and admin scope; until then the gates-ran evaluator still demands every leaf the summary names, so enforcement is unchanged.

main: required checks the policy declare.reason: Same class as the develop record: main's live ruleset lags the declared policy by these checks (the four new coverage producers plus six pre-existing). Recorded rather than reconciled; enforcement through the summaries and gates-ran is unchanged.

$comment: Checks deliberately non-required must be named here with a reason.
advisory.pr-base: PR-only branch-policy check (#383): reports on pull_request events only, so it cannot be a required check that the merge queue waits on (merge_group); the correction is to rebase onto develop.
advisory.DevSkim: devskim.yml triggers on push/pull_request/schedule only, no merge_group -- same structural gap as pr-base. It runs on every develop PR but remains advisory until the owner explicitly adds it to the required merge contract; a merge-queue entry must not wait for a status this check never reports there.
advisory.Mutation gate (changed critical lines): mutation.yml's pull_request trigger carries a paths filter (packages/**/*.py and the mutation governance artifacts), so PRs outside the filter never see the check report and branch protection cannot require it without waiting on `Expected` forever -- the same paths-scope rule #162 already encodes. The gate still blocks its own diffs: it fails closed on zero mutants, zero selected tests, missing tooling, timeout-infrastructure failure, or an unreadable trusted base, and #330's nightly (mutation-nightly.yml) measures the full critical set. Promote it to required only by dropping the paths filter first.
